# Deploy on one VM with Docker Compose

The fastest production-shaped deployment: one virtual machine, four containers. It runs the same on an OVHcloud or Hetzner VPS, an EC2 instance, a Compute Engine or Azure VM. For several agents or a team, prefer [Kubernetes with Helm](./12-kubernetes-helm.mdx).

## Goal

A VS Agent reachable at `https://agent.example.com`, with its admin API bound to the host only, data on named volumes, TLS handled automatically.

## Prerequisites

- A VM with Docker Engine and the Compose plugin, ports 80 and 443 open, 2 GB of memory.
- A DNS A or AAAA record for your hostname pointing at the VM.
- The values of [What VS Agent needs to run](./10-requirements.mdx) decided.

## Steps

### 1. Lay out the files

Create a directory with three files. The Compose file:

<CodeBlock language="yaml" title="examples/vs-11-docker-compose/docker-compose.yml">{Compose}</CodeBlock>

The TLS proxy configuration, with your hostname:

<CodeBlock language="text" title="examples/vs-11-docker-compose/Caddyfile">{Caddy}</CodeBlock>

The environment, copied to `.env` and filled in:

<CodeBlock language="bash" title="examples/vs-11-docker-compose/.env.example">{Env}</CodeBlock>

### 2. Generate the agent's mnemonic

Any BIP-39 generator works; `veranad keys add agent --keyring-backend test` prints one and the matching address. Put the mnemonic in `.env`, store it in your secret manager, and never commit the file. Fund the address with a few test coins.

### 3. Start

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f vs-agent
```

The first start creates the DID and publishes the DID Document; later starts load it.

## Verify

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/agent/health/ready          # 200
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/v2/agent/info | jq              # did, version
curl -s https://agent.example.com/.well-known/did.json | jq .id  # the same DID, from the internet
```

The DID Document must be reachable over HTTPS from outside the VM, otherwise nobody can resolve you.

## Operations

- **Upgrade**: change `VS_AGENT_VERSION` in `.env`, `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. Read the release notes first; see [Upgrade VS Agent](./104-upgrade.mdx).
- **Backup**: the `postgres-data` and `agent-data` volumes, plus `.env`. See [Back up and restore](./102-backup-restore.mdx).
- **Logs**: `docker compose logs`; levels through `AGENT_LOG_LEVEL` and `ADMIN_API_LOG_LEVEL`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Caddy cannot obtain a certificate | DNS does not point at the VM yet, or port 80 is closed | Fix DNS or the firewall, restart Caddy |
| Agent exits at start naming a variable | A required variable is missing or invalid | Compare with the `.env.example` |
| Agent exits saying the DID location differs | `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` changed after first start | Restore the original value |
| Admin API answers `403` from your backend | The backend's address is outside `ADMIN_API_TRUSTED_NETWORKS` | Add its network, or switch to corporation mode |
